test_title: PYST 3: Selection Post (Higher Secondary Level) - GA (Held On 31 July, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: If someone becomes a minister or the Prime Minister without being a Member of Parliament, they must get elected to the Parliament within _______ months or they will have to vacate the office.
solution:
The correct answer is __**six months**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 75(5)** of the **Indian Constitution** states that a person who is not a Member of Parliament (MP) can still be appointed as a minister, including the **Prime Minister**. However, such a person must become an MP within a period of **six months** from the date of their appointment.
 
• If the appointed person fails to get elected to either the **Lok Sabha** or the **Rajya Sabha** within this six-month period, they must resign from their ministerial position. Hence, option 2 is correct.
 
• This provision ensures that the **executive branch** remains accountable to the legislative branch, which is a crucial aspect of the **parliamentary system of governance**.
 
• The rule applies to both the **Union government** (Prime Minister and Union Ministers) and the **state governments** (Chief Ministers and State Ministers).
 
• The six-month provision allows flexibility in governance, ensuring that capable individuals can assume key positions temporarily even if they are not immediately elected members of the legislature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 75 of the Indian Constitution:**

 
 
• **Article 75(1):** It states that the Prime Minister is appointed by the President, and the other ministers are appointed on the advice of the Prime Minister.
 
• **Article 75(5):** It mandates that a minister who is not a member of either House of Parliament must become a member within six months of their appointment.
 
• This article ensures that the **executive branch** is accountable to the **legislature**, which is a cornerstone of India's parliamentary democracy.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Application:**
 
 
• **PV Narasimha Rao:** He was appointed as the **Prime Minister** in 1991 and contested elections to become a member of the Parliament within six months.
 
• **Jayalalithaa:** In 2001, she was sworn in as the Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu but had to resign after being disqualified from contesting elections.
 
 
 
• **Parliamentary System of Government:**
 
 
• India follows a **parliamentary system of governance**, where the executive is responsible to the legislature.
 
• The system ensures that ministers, including the Prime Minister, remain answerable to the Parliament, reinforcing the principles of **democracy** and **accountability**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Legal Considerations:**

 
 
• The six-month provision is crucial in allowing the government to function smoothly while ensuring that all executive members hold a legitimate mandate from the legislature.
 
• The **President of India** plays a key role in appointing ministers, including individuals who are not MPs, based on the advice of the Prime Minister.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Six-Month Rule:**
 
 
• It provides a mechanism for appointing non-legislators as ministers or Prime Minister temporarily, ensuring that governance is not hindered.
 
• This provision has been used multiple times in India, highlighting its practical importance in the country's political framework.
